title: Cover Design: Quality Publications
slide_intent: Teach designers to plan the front and back as one visual package. A cover image can invite a reader into the subject before the text begins.
strategic_value: NASA can give major publications a distinctive presence while crediting the agency and mission separately.
demonstration: Two large cover examples use dense equation imagery and an illuminated planetary crescent. A smaller pair shows the back and front together. The note specifies four-color originals, although the manual reproduces these illustrations in monochrome.
practical_value: Review a proposed image at cover scale, then inspect the front and back together to decide where the mission patch and agency identification belong.

content_islands.name: Cover concept guidance
content_islands.spec: Use the top columns for image quality, front/back planning and the note about the monochrome reproduction.

content_islands.name: Large cover treatments
content_islands.spec: Pair two images at equal scale to show how a dense surface or a mostly dark field can support a title and identification.

content_islands.name: Front and back pair
content_islands.spec: Below the main examples, label the smaller back and front covers. Keep the patch, signature and image placements visible in relation to the whole package.
